title: Lift a flush access cover out of its frame with twist-lock lifting keys
instruction: Lift the grey access cover out of its frame with the lifting keys, lay it flat across the two blue bearers, then draw the keys out.
context: Utility and facilities workers lift flush floor-duct, meter-pit and valve-chamber covers with lifting keys: the key goes through a slot, is turned a quarter turn to catch under the cover, and lifts it; the cover is laid on bearers so no key or finger is trapped. Unlike TK-DXNUXC (two tools slid under a load, lifted onto bearers) and TK-7AHCHJ (tiles lifted by finger slots), each tool must be lined up with a slot and turned to engage, and the load comes straight up out of a tight frame.
setup: World frame: x is forward from the arm bases, y to the robot's left, heights above the table top; the midline is halfway between the two arm bases. Access frame (fixed, dark grey cast iron), centred 380 mm in front of the arm bases on the midline: 170 mm front to back, 294 mm side to side, 40 mm tall, with 15 mm walls round an opening 140 x 264 mm. Inside the walls a ledge 5 mm wide and 10 mm deep runs all round, its top 30 mm above the table; below it is only the table. Cover (loose, grey glass-fibre composite, 0.6 kg): 136 mm front to back, 260 mm side to side, 10 mm thick, resting on the ledge with its top flush with the frame and a 2 mm gap all round. Two cross-shaped keyholes go through it, centred 100 mm left and 100 mm right of the cover's centre: each is a 14 mm square with a narrow slot through it, 8 mm front to back and 30 mm side to side. Two bearers (fixed, blue painted timber), each 20 mm front to back, 270 mm side to side and 20 mm tall, centred on the midline 175 mm and 275 mm in front of the arm bases. Two lifting keys (loose, 0.06 kg each), each 96 mm tall: a steel crossbar 4 mm front to back, 26 mm side to side and 6 mm tall at the foot, a 10 mm round steel shaft 70 mm long, and a yellow plastic 20 mm cube handle on top. Each stands upright, crossbar side to side, in a key holder (fixed, dark plastic sleeve 30 mm tall, 14 x 32 mm inside with the long side side to side, 4 mm walls) centred 300 mm in front of the arm bases and 195 mm left or right of the midline. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Pass/fail. Score 1.0: the cover lies flat across both bearers, either face down, every corner of its underside within 1.5 mm of the bearer tops (20 mm above the table), its centre within 25 mm front to back and 30 mm side to side of the point midway between the bearers, still and released; neither key passes through it (a key lying on top of it is fine); and the cover was never dropped from more than 30 mm during the trial (judged from the video). Score 0 in every other case: the cover still in or on the frame (lifted, tilted or seated), on the table, propped, resting on a key, tilted more than 3 degrees, held above the bearers, a key still through it, or dropped at any time. The trial ends at 1.0 once the 1.0 condition has held for 1 s; otherwise it scores the state at the last step.
reset_notes: Seat the cover back on the frame's ledge, flush and centred (2 mm gap all round), and stand each key upright in its holder with its crossbar side to side. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Rigid boxes and cylinders in PhysX, friction 1.2 static and 1.0 dynamic on the cover, keys, frame and holders. The cover, keys and frame are bench-scale: real keys are longer with T-handles, and these are gripped by a handle block and turned by the wrist. The cover is a light composite one; nothing (dirt, a seal or corrosion) holds it in the frame beyond its weight.
